kind: Parallel assistant implementation and interoperability review; not a human or installed-plugin certification

resolved_findings.finding: Native-derived snapshots missed existing logical DOCX edge loss.
resolved_findings.resolution: Independent retained fixture hash and raw-source four-edge oracle; modern and legacy leading/trailing declarations map after effective table direction; inverse save mapping.

resolved_findings.finding: Foreign table-style selectors or foreign/nested table properties could choose an inherited RTL direction.
resolved_findings.resolution: Native namespace and direct-depth checks; targeted foreign-selector, foreign-container and nested-container regressions.

resolved_findings.finding: Borderless explicit off masks could share a style-cache entry with absent sides.
resolved_findings.resolution: Cache identity retains raw off-mask distinction when no common stroke is visible.

resolved_findings.finding: Uniform halfstroke padding compensation was not supported by actual converter geometry.
resolved_findings.resolution: Retain modeled padding; archive controlled actual conversion/PDF measurements separately.

reviewed_contracts: ODT border shorthand resets precede same-layer side overrides and inherited defaults.
Supported tables use one opaque RGB solid stroke at exact eighth-point widths from 0.25 through 12 pt.
Visible ODT input requires effective collapsing border model; unsupported mixed/styled/covered structures refuse.
Merged ownership and nested-table independence survive supported conversion.
Explicit direct off overrides inherited/default RTL; modern start/end take precedence regardless of order.
Editable ODT refuses unsupported RTL table column order while paragraph RTL remains separate.
Field-boundary source properties and opaque revision-history code are not modified by the border alias correction.
limits: No arbitrary external DOCX per-cell stroke fidelity claim.
No installed Zotero-plugin or Microsoft Word acceptance.
No unrestricted ODF, stable LibreOffice qualification or pixel-equivalent rendering claim.
